draft.title: The fall of the Western Roman Empire
card: By the 300s CE the Roman Empire was split into a western half and an eastern half, each with its own emperor. The western half was ruled from Italy.

Several pressures built up in the west. Groups from outside the empire, such as the Goths and Vandals, invaded. Many emperors were weak and ruled for only a short time. The government also had money troubles, because it struggled to pay for armies and officials.
In 476 CE the last western emperor was removed from power. This date is used to mark the end of Roman rule in western Europe. Historians say several causes worked together, not just one.
The eastern half, called the Eastern Empire or Byzantium, did not fall then. It lasted about another thousand years.
draft.remember: The west fell in 476 CE after several pressures combined, but the east carried on.

a.q: Which statement best explains why Roman rule ended in western Europe?
opts: Invasions, weak rulers and money troubles all added up
A single invasion by the Goths destroyed the whole empire
The empire chose to give up its western lands in 476 CE
Money troubles alone left the army with nothing to do
a.why: The card says invasions, weak emperors and money troubles all built up in the west, and that historians see several causes working together. Blaming a single invasion is tempting, but it leaves out the other pressures and the way they combined.
a.clue: Think about how many causes the card names.

b.q: A student says, 'The Roman Empire ended completely in 476 CE.' Why is this claim wrong?
opts: The Eastern Empire, Byzantium, lasted about 1000 more years
Rome's rule in western Europe carried on after 476 CE
The empire had already ended in the east before 476 CE
Byzantium was the name of the western half of the empire
b.why: The year 476 CE marks the end of Roman rule in the west only. The eastern half, Byzantium, lasted about another thousand years. The claim treats the end of the west as the end of the whole empire.
b.clue: Remember that the empire had two halves.

a.best: Invasions, weak rulers and money troubles all added up

b.best: The Eastern Empire, Byzantium, lasted about 1000 more years
